move: three mono phones flip 180 in a ripple, rest, flip again
how: Three 250x520 two-faced cards (white front / black back, backface-visibility hidden) sit in a row with a screen-blend SVG grain overlay. At 6% of the 5s each card flips rotateY 0 -> 180 over 1.1s with expo.inOut, staggered 0.18s so the row ripples; at 56% they flip 180 -> 360 the same way, so after two half-turns every card is back at its front. Meanwhile the whole row leans rotateX 6 -> -4 and rotateY -8 -> 8 with sine.inOut over 2.5s and yoyos back, and each card bobs y 0 -> -14 with a staggered yoyo, both mirrored so the loop closes.
adapt: Replace the six screen templates (three fronts, three backs), the caption and index text; the palette is deliberately black and white so change the grain opacity rather than adding colour. Keep the 1.1s expo.inOut flips at 0.06 and 0.56 of the duration with 0.18s stagger.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the .row with three .flip cards from shot.screens plus the grain SVG; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with flips at 0.06D and 0.56D and the yoyo lean/bob of duration D/2 repeat 1. The second flip already uses immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1600px and the grain feTurbulence filter covers the full frame.
caveats: full-frame feTurbulence grain with mix-blend-mode screen adds per-frame cost
catalog has no jitter source; the design is original
